Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

 Community Resources Carpenter, Director of IT Guadagnino, Director of Economic & Community
 Development Jimenez, Director of Public Works Delgadillo, Deputy City Manager Anda-Scaia, Chief Deputy
 City Clerk Garcia, Library Services Manager Hassen.

 The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Ramon and Mari Cruz.

 The Invocation was led by Councilmember Beckwith.

 CLOSED SESSION REPORT

 City Attorney Marco Martinez reported City Council met in closed session for four items and reported there were
 no reportable actions for any of the four items. There will be future discussions at future meetings regarding two
 items related to Item 3.

 CEREMONIAL

 1.  Presentation of Certificates of Appreciation to all who contributed to the 2024 Kathy’s Cool Cuts for Kids
 Event

 Mayor Gonzales presented Certificates of Appreciation to all who contributed to the 2024 Kathy’s Cool Cuts for
 Kids Event.

 2.  Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming the week of September 16-20, 2024 as National Adult & Family
 Literacy Week in the City of Azusa

 Councilmember Beckwith read aloud the Proclamation proclaiming the week of September 16-20, 2024 as
 National Adult & Family Literacy Week in the City of Azusa.

 3.  Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming September 15 – October 15, 2024 as Hispanic Heritage Month
 in the City of Azusa

 Mayor Pro-Tem Alvarez read aloud the Proclamation proclaiming September 15 – October 15, 2024 as Hispanic
 Heritage Month in the City of Azusa.

 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

 Diana Reyes Williams, President of the Azusa Woman’s Club, shared that the Azusa Woman’s club will be
 hosting a Bunco event on Sunday, September 22, 2024 at 1:00 p.m. The cost is $20, and the money raised will go
 to the club’s scholarship fund. Last year, the club gave $4,000 dollars to four graduating seniors from Azusa, and
 the club hopes to raise enough to give another $4,000 dollars or more in June.

 Alexandra M. invited the community to attend the the Azusa Woman’s Club Gatsby Night Scholarship
 Fundraiser event on Saturday, October 12, 2024. She thanked the Azusa Golden Days Committee for their
 undying dedication to celebrate the beautiful City of Azusa and for their inclusivity of all non-profit
 organizations that support the community members. The Azusa Woman’s Club was proud to confer four $1,000
 dollar scholarships to four very deserving students at Azusa High School last June, and the club looks forward to
 awarding four or more next June. She encouraged the community to dust off their flapper dresses and dapper
 suits or go shopping for an outfit and celebrate the spirit of Azusa Golden Days and bring the spirit of giving.
 Presale tickets are $50 per person until September 27, 2024, and then tickets will be $60 per person and $65 at
 the door. Reach out to a member of the Azusa Woman’s Club or call (626) 536-1701 for tickets.

 Christina Ramirez, Azusa Connects Co-Founder, invited the community to the Azusa Golden Days Chalk Fest 3
 event. The festival will have chalk to jazz up the Memorial Park parking lot, along with music, vendors, and
 food. Artists can register online, and the chalk walk to view the art will be open from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. on
 Sunday, October 13, 2024.

City Council June 17, 2024  Page | 2
  Kim Antel invited the community to help kids from pre-kindergarten through high school with their homework.
 The community can help the children understand mathematics or how to sound out words, read, and spell. She
 provided examples of what she has done to be a part of a homework house, and encouraged the community to
 join her by contacting the Neighborhood Homework House at (626) 969-7051.

 REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

 1.  ‘Pet of the Month’ Presentation by Los Angeles County Animal Care & Control

 Councilmember Avila Jr. presented a flyer for Llorona, a six-month-old, tan and spayed Husky mix. Llorona
 loves playing and cuddling, and she is available for adoption at the Baldwin Park Animal Care Center.

 2.  City Manager Communications
 •  Progress report of the Azusa Resource Center, located at 975 W. Foothill Blvd.

 City Manager Gonzalez announced that the Council will be asked to select the winning name for the City’s
 newest dog park at the next meeting. Second phase construction of the major rehabilitation of Foothill and Alosta
 is underway. He congratulated Lucy Demirjian for shepherding the Azusa Resource Center Project.

 Lucy Demirjian, Senior Project Manager, provided a brief presentation regarding the status of the Azusa
 Resource Center and responded to Council questions and comments.

 3.  Economic and Community Development Department Update

 Director of Economic & Community Development Jose Jimenez introduced Linda Hinojos, Economic
 Development Specialist, who provided a brief update on the Economic & Community Development Department
 in the City of Azusa.

 Director of Economic & Community Development Jimenez presented slides regarding the Small Business
 Support Grant 2.0 program and responded to Council questions.

 COUNCIL COMMENTS

 Mayor Gonzales announced that he was invited to Representative Grace Napolitano’s Retirement Dinner event
 and asked for staff to plan something nice to provide to her. The annual Azusa Shred-a-Thon event is scheduled
 for September 21, 2024 at the Azusa Light & Water Parking Lot. The City’s free compost and mulch giveaway is
 scheduled for September 28, 2024 at Memorial Park from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m.

 Mayor Pro-Tem Alvarez announced the Azusa City Library would be celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month on
 September 25, 2024 from 6 p.m. to 7 p.m. Crafts, activities, and refreshments will be available for the whole

 has incredible chile rellenos. He provided a shoutout to Soleful Steps Shoes & Accessories, a local women’s
 accessories business.

 community out of harms way. Thanks to the staff, police department, veteran groups, and the Azusa Rotary Club
 for the Field of Glory ceremony. Thanks to staff for the cooling centers during the hot week. The press
 conference for the riverbed funding was a great event. He reported attending the Gold Line JPA as an alternate
 and as reported, they are on time and on budget. He announced a wonderful opportunity to meet author Annette
 Chavez Macias on September 18, 2024.

 the City of Azusa for over twenty years. He encouraged anyone free from 3:15 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Mondays
 and/or Wednesdays or on Tuesdays and/or Thursdays to call the Neighborhood Homework House to become part
 of the same miracle stories and help volunteer. He thanked Kim Antel for her assistance with the Neighborhood
 Homework House. There is a free tire collection event on September 21, 2024 from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. located at
 the S2 Lot of Citrus College. He reported attending the Contract City’s Conference the first weekend of this
 month in Ocean Side. His favorite event was the mental health segment covered on four elected officials. He
 voiced his thoughts on some of the Gold Line struggles with two county supervisors who attended. He requested
 a certificate for the Azusa Little League Majors for winning the District 19 Championship. He urged the
 community to visit the Soleful Steps business.
